chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said,
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who abandons his wife without a divorce or an oath, for a year, not approaching her bed. He (peace be upon him) said: Let him go to his wife.

And he (peace be upon him) said: Whichever man solemnly oaths from his wife, and the solemn oath is that he says, 'No, by Allah, I will not sleep with you, such and such', and he says, 'By Allah, I shall constrict you (due to my anger with you)', then he is angry with her, so he awaits with her for four months.
Then he should be seized by it, after four months. So he pauses, and he meets and the meeting is that he reconciles with his wife, so Allah (azwj) is most Forgiving more Merciful.

So if he does not meet, he is compelled that he divorces, and a divorce does not happen between the two of them until he pauses, even if it was as well after the four months, he would be compelled upon that he either meets (reconciles) or divorces.

key_terms.إِيلَاء: Solemn oath of abstention from sexual intercourse

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and procedure for a husband who takes an oath to abstain from his wife?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudence of 'al-ila' (solemn oath of abstention), distinguishing it from simple separation by mandating a four-month waiting period before the husband is compelled to either resume conjugal relations or effect a divorce. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the husband's obligation to 'fa'' (reconcile) or 'talaq' (divorce) to prevent indefinite limbo, ensuring the wife's rights are protected through judicial or communal enforcement.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who abandons his wife from without a divorce and oaths that for a year he would not go near her bed’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Let him go to his wife’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whichever man solemnly oaths from his wife, and the solemn oath is that he is saying, ‘No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, I will not sleep with you, such and such’, and he is saying, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, I shall constrict you (due to my anger with you), then he is angry with her, so he awaits with her for four months.
Then he should be seized by it, after four months. So he pauses, and he meets and the meeting is that he reconciles with his wife, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is most Forgiving more Merciful.

So if he does not meet, he is compelled that he divorces, and a divorce does not happen between the two of them until he pauses, even if it was as well after the four months, he would be compelled upon that he either meets (reconciles) or divorces’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who separates from his wife without divorce and swearing. He does not go near her bed for one year. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must go to his wife.’

He (the Imam) then said, ‘If one swears about his wife, it takes place by one’s saying, “No, by Allah, I will not have sexual intercourse with you so and so, and say, by Allah I must reduce you” and then become angry with her. He can wait for four months.
After four months, he must be taken in custody, so that he may reach reconciliation with his wife; Allah is forgiving and merciful.

If he does not reach a settlement, he then is made to divorce. Divorce cannot take place until he is placed under custody. If it is after four months, still he is made to reach a settlement or divorce.’”
